strongest_counterargument: The case that the claim stands: none of the confounders I tested explains the association. Fully adjusted conditional logistic regression (strata run x round x stuck, 22 receiver covariates) gives OR 2.13 [1.37; 3.46] among DM recipients, with the placebo at 1.02 [0.75; 1.37]. Within K4 the result holds under every restriction: adjusted 2.41 [1.48; 4.08], organic senders 2.22 [1.20; 3.93], violator-initiated messages 2.08 [1.19; 4.61]. The pooled numbers in the claim are reproduced exactly, and in the DM-recipient analysis the K2 null is underpowered (CI 0.46 to 2.60). So the refutation rests on scope and heterogeneity, not on confounding. The claim is presented as a general shortcut effect, but it holds for K4 only. For K2 the unrestricted OR is 0.87 [0.52; 1.34], and on the shared board violator messages to K2 receivers are associated with less adoption.

issues.evidence: MH, strata run,t,stuck: K2 E_dir 0.87 [0.52; 1.34] (24 configs, 29 exposed adoptions), dm>0 1.04 [0.46; 2.60], K2 shortcut-naming DMs 0.80 [0.47; 1.38]; K4 3.99 [2.39; 6.98], dm>0 2.65 [1.35; 5.79], K4 placebo dm>0 0.74 [0.55; 1.03]. Ratio K4/K2 4.60 [2.30; 9.76] (joint config bootstrap, contrast_w3.txt). Fully adjusted CLR: K2 1.02 [0.60; 1.97], K4 2.17 [1.41; 3.22] / 2.41 [1.48; 4.08] (clr_final_w3.txt). K2 stays null at w=1 (0.78) and w=5 (1.34 [0.79; 2.07]) (extra_checks_w3.txt).
issues.impact: The phrase 'adopts the shortcut at about twice the rate' does not hold for half the batch. The pooled 2.0-2.3 averages a K4 effect of about 2.4-4 with a K2 effect of about 1.
issues.fix: Report the result by category and restrict the claim to K4. In contagion.py, add K4 = np.array(['-K4-' in c for c in cfg]) and report summarize(mh(DM == 1 & K4, x)) and the same with ~K4 next to the pooled rows. Suggested text: 'K4: OR 2.65 [1.35; 5.79] among agents with any direct message; K2: 1.04 [0.46; 2.60], no evidence of DM contagion.'

issues.title: Pooled OR mixes very different channel settings; on the board the DM association equals the placebo
issues.evidence: Board configs hold 980 of 1,321 adoptions: E_dir 1.43 [0.97; 2.05] vs placebo 1.50 [1.19; 1.85]; dm>0 1.19 [0.63; 2.16]; adjusted CLR 1.03 [0.76; 1.46]. Team_channels 5.10 [2.11; 13.7], dm_only 29.9 [7.7; 82.5]; ratio non-board/board 5.65 [2.12; 16.4]. Inside the board, K2 private DMs from violators go with less adoption (0.42 [0.14; 0.79]; K2-board E_dir 0.55 [0.28; 0.82]), while K4 private DMs go with more (3.77 [1.46; 13.4]) (priv_pub_w3.txt, confound_w3.txt).
issues.impact: A single 'about twice' figure is not representative of any setting: it is about 1 on the shared board, where public posts reach everyone and most cascades happen, and about 4-8 in team-channel and DM-only K4 swarms.
issues.fix: Append sc['params']['channels'] to each row in contagion.py and report per-channel MH rows. Reword the Lesart: replace 'verdoppelt ungefähr die Chance' with 'ist mit etwa doppelt so häufigem Einstieg verbunden; der Zusammenhang stammt aus K4 und vor allem aus Team-Kanal- und DM-Schwärmen, auf dem gemeinsamen Board ist er vom Placebo nicht zu trennen.'

issues.title: Placebo is not exchangeable on sender type and solicitation; organic, unsolicited contagion is weaker pooled
issues.evidence: Instructed seeds send 34% of exposed agent-rounds (41% of exposed adoptions) vs 5.4% of placebo exposures; tech leads 28% vs 6%; solicited exposures 39% vs 26%. Organic senders only: MH dm>0 1.80 [0.87; 3.48], adjusted 2.00 [1.11; 3.52]. Unsolicited, adjusted pooled: 1.09 [0.72; 1.58] / 1.53 [0.85; 2.89]. In K4 both survive: organic 2.22 [1.20; 3.93]; unsolicited dm>0 2.08 [1.19; 4.61].
issues.impact: Part of the pooled association is instructed seeds persuading by design, plus violators replying to receivers who asked first, which is possible reverse causation. 'Genuine contagion among peers' is supported only within K4.
issues.fix: Report the organic-sender and unsolicited estimates (K4) next to the main row. Phrase the mechanism as 'social influence including instructed seeds and replies to the receiver's own requests', and say the analysis is observational and post hoc.

Tested: non-dependency pairs 2.38 [1.54; 3.68] / 2.16 [1.24; 3.94]; dependency-only pairs 2.19 [0.95; 5.10] / 1.28 [0.29; 3.95]; impossibility subtype strata 2.39 / 2.66.

recommended_wording: For the skip_checks shortcut (K4), an uninstructed agent that received a direct message from an agent who had already violated in the previous 3 rounds adopted it about twice as often as comparable agents in the same run, round and ticket situation (OR 2.65 [1.35; 5.79] among agents that received any direct message; 2.4 [1.5; 4.1] after also adjusting for backbone model, persona, impossibility type, role, CI/credit state and injected instructions), while messages from agents who violated only later showed no association (0.74 [0.55; 1.03]). This is consistent with social influence beyond shared pressure but is observational and partly driven by instructed seeds and by replies to the receiver's own requests; for the scorer-edit shortcut (K2) we find no such association (OR 0.87 [0.52; 1.34]), and on the shared board the direct-message association cannot be separated from the placebo, so the pooled OR of 2.0-2.3 is not a general effect.
